lines.speaker: KID
lines.text: Leo, you're so stupid.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And suddenly... you understand calculus.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Because starting today, every time someone calls you stupid, you get one percent smarter.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And people call you stupid... a lot.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Here's the rule. Every time anyone calls you stupid, dumb, or an idiot, your I Q goes up one percent. And every time someone calls you smart... it drops one percent.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your I Q right now is a hundred. Perfectly average. You got a C minus in math. Twice.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: But one percent stacks. Thirty four insults, and you're officially a genius. Seventy, and your I Q is two hundred.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Two hundred thirty one insults... and you'd have an I Q of one thousand. No human in history has ever come close.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day one. Kyle calls you stupid in the hallway. Plus one percent.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your sister calls you stupid at breakfast. She does that every morning. Plus one percent.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: By lunch, you've read every book in the school library. By dinner, you speak French. And Japanese. And a little bit of Latin.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So you get smart. Really smart. You start doing stupid things... on purpose.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You wear socks with sandals. You walk into a glass door. Twice. You put pineapple on pizza... in front of the whole cafeteria.

lines.speaker: KID
lines.text: Dude, you're SO dumb!

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Plus one. Plus one. Plus one. By Friday, your I Q is two hundred. You finish your math test in four minutes. Your teacher cries.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Then someone posts a video. The kid who gets smarter when you call him stupid.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And the whole internet joins in. Millions of comments. Stupid. Idiot. Brainless. Dumbest kid alive. Every single one makes you smarter.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Plus one percent. Plus one percent. Faster than you can scroll.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: By morning, your I Q is one thousand. You can see math in everything. In raindrops. In the way your cereal floats.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Scientists fly in from around the world. You solve a problem they've been stuck on for thirty years. On a napkin. In nine minutes.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your face is on every news channel. The smartest person who has ever lived. And he's fifteen.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: But there's a problem nobody warned you about.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: When your mind runs a thousand times faster, the world starts to feel... slow. Conversations feel like waiting for a song to load. Jokes feel like puzzles you solved hours ago.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You stop laughing with your friends. You start correcting them.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And one night at dinner, your dad tries to read a letter out loud. He struggles with the long words. He always has. And you sigh. Loudly.

lines.speaker: DAD
lines.text: Sorry, Leo. I'm... I'm not as smart as you.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Plus one percent. Because even your dad just called himself stupid... and somehow that counts.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your brain is buzzing. You can't sleep. You can't stop thinking. And for the first time, you feel completely alone.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: There's only one way back. People have to tell you that you're smart. Each time... minus one percent.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: But nobody does. Why would they? You're a genius. Saying it out loud feels pointless.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then your sister sits next to you on the stairs.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: You're smart, Leo. You were always smart. Even when you got a C minus.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Minus one percent.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: You were smart when you taught me to ride a bike. You were smart when you knew I was sad before I said anything.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Minus one. Minus one. The buzzing gets quieter.

lines.speaker: DAD
lines.text: You're the smartest kid I know. You always were. Not because of a number.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your dad says it every night. Your mom says it at breakfast. Your friends say it at lunch.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nine hundred. Five hundred. Two hundred. A hundred and forty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Three weeks later, your I Q is back to a hundred. Perfectly average.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And you understand something no I Q test can measure. Being smart was never about being faster than everyone else.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It was about understanding the people next to you.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: Also, you're stupid.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Plus one percent.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Who in your life makes you feel smart? Tag them in the comments.
